LESSON: COMMON SOLIDS

Grade: Grade 8
Subject: MATHEMATICS
Strand: Geometry 4.3 Scale Drawing (14 lessons) • Scale length • Conversions in scale • 
Topic 4.4: Common Solids
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 16

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Common Solids, part of Geometry 4.3 Scale Drawing (14 lessons) • Scale length • Conversions in scale •  in Grade 8 MATHEMATICS.

Key inquiry question: What are common solids? 2. How do we use common solids in real life?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

A. Suggested learning experiences (from KICD)

1. identify and collect common solids such as cubes, cuboids, cylinders, pyramids and cones from the immediate environment,

2. discuss, open and sketch the nets of hollow solids,

3. work out the surface area of solids from nets,

4. discuss and practice measuring the distance between any two points on the surface of the solids,

5. make models of hollow and compact solids using locally available materials such as clay. Hollow solids (containers) may be of cubes, cuboids, cylinders, pyramids, cones or pots. Compact solids (eg. bricks) may 1.

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

1. identify and collect common solids such as cubes, cuboids, cylinders, pyramids and cones from the immediate environment,
2. discuss, open and sketch the nets of hollow solids,
3. work out the surface area of solids from nets,
4. discuss and practice measuring the distance between any two points on the surface of the solids,
5. make models of hollow and compact solids using locally available materials such as clay. Hollow solids (containers) may be of cubes, cuboids, cylinders, pyramids, cones or pots. Compact solids (eg. bricks) may 1.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Common Solids together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
• Communication and Collaboration: as the learner discusses and works with peers to collect solids from the environment.

• Creativity and Imagination: as the learner makes the models of different solids.

Values

Responsibility, love and respect: as the learner works with peers to collect solids and make models.

Values:

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs):

• ESD: as the learner collects solids from the environment and use locally available materials to make models.

• Self-esteem: as the learner engages to open nets of solids and makes models creatively.

Link to other learning areas

• Pre-Technical Studies: as the leaner enhances drawing skills as they sketch nets of different solids.

• Creative Art and Sports: as the learner uses creative skills to make models of different solids.
